builder_plan.change: Test the proposed division of work against a single-agent implementation.
builder_plan.baseline: One agent with the same tools and an equal total token and time budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Accepted outputs, coordination failures, wall-clock time, and total cost across all agents.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Ask on Demand: Targeted Peer Communication for Parallel Agentic Systems
summary: Ask on Demand replaces pre-emptive sharing and summarization with a pull-based mechanism where agents query peers for specific evidence only when needed. It requires training a lightweight gate using paired team continuations and final outcome labels, which adds pipeline complexity and implementation overhead beyond standard API-based agent frameworks. The gate can fail to approve necessary queries or approve wasteful ones, and the approach depends on maintaining accessible peer execution histories at inference time.
rationale: The method requires training a custom gating model and maintaining peer history infrastructure, which exceeds typical constrained-infrastructure capabilities despite the promised cost savings.
technique: On-demand peer querying for parallel LLM agents

claims.statement: Ask on Demand replaces pre-emptive sharing and summarization with a pull-based mechanism where agents query peers for specific evidence only when needed. It requires training a lightweight gate using paired team continuations and final outcome labels, which adds pipeline complexity and implementation overhead beyond standard API-based agent frameworks. The gate can fail to approve necessary queries or approve wasteful ones, and the approach depends on maintaining accessible peer execution histories at inference time.
AOD consistently improves task performance over independent parallel execution while achieving lower inference cost than existing information-sharing baselines.
